record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: For grading-restricted vertex algebras, what conditions make formal deformations converge to analytic deformations, and can the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras be generalized to genus-zero full conformal field theories?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Find the conditions for the formal deformations of grading-restricted vertex algebras to converge to analytic deformations. Generalize the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras to a deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal field theories.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let V = ⊕_{n∈ℤ} V_{(n)} be a grading-restricted vertex algebra over ℂ (i.e., dim V_{(n)} < ∞ for all n and V_{(n)} = 0 for n sufficiently negative), equipped with vertex operator map Y: V ⊗ V → V((x)), vacuum 𝟙, and conformal vector ω. A formal deformation of V is a family of vertex operator maps Y_κ = Y + Σ_{i≥1} κ^i Y^{(i)} (with Y^{(i)}: V ⊗ V → V((x))) parameterized by a formal variable κ that satisfies the vertex algebra axioms as a formal power series in κ. An analytic deformation is such a family for which the formal series in κ converges (in a suitable topology) for κ in some neighborhood of 0 in ℂ, yielding an actual vertex algebra for each such κ.

(a) Identify natural sufficient conditions (cohomological, analytic, or otherwise) on V and on the formal deformation Y_κ under which the formal deformation converges to an analytic deformation.

(b) A genus-zero full conformal field theory consists of a graded vector space H together with a system of correlation-function maps for points on the Riemann sphere satisfying associativity, commutativity, and other genus-zero sewing/duality axioms (combining holomorphic and antiholomorphic vertex algebra structures). Develop a deformation theory (including the appropriate notion of formal deformation, an obstruction/cohomology framework, and conditions for convergence) for genus-zero full conformal field theories that generalizes the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras.
artifact.status_search_result: A search returns Huang's cohomology theory for grading-restricted vertex algebras and subsequent generalizations (e.g., to vertex superalgebras in 2025), where the relevant second cohomology classifies first-order/formal deformations. No source establishes general sufficient conditions for convergence of formal deformations to analytic ones, nor a full deformation theory for genus-zero full conformal field theories generalizing the vertex-algebra case. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A cohomology theory of supercommutative algebras and grading-restricted vertex superalgebras
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes Huang's cohomology theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras; second cohomology classifies square-zero extensions and first-order deformations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work develops cohomological deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex (super)algebras but does not resolve convergence of formal to analytic deformations.

status_evidence.title: A Cohomology Theory of Grading-Restricted Vertex Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Huang's framework where H^2 governs first-order deformations of vertex algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The foundational deformation-cohomology theory exists, but convergence and the full-CFT generalization are not addressed.
